driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle fired the morning of 1 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions pre-open fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-09-30.json from Wednesday 30 September's close. Every figure recorded here is dated at or before the 2026-09-30 close; news-log entries dated 1 October (10-year at 5.33%, Micron-led chip rally, Brent above $100) and the AAII survey for the week ending 30 September were deliberately not used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale: bonds 15 (TLT 30-day implied volatility, 25 September), dollar 4.72 (EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility, 21 September), IWM 19.97 (RVX, 23 September). No newer prints were obtainable.

Source conflicts on 30 September: the news log has the S&P 500 cash index at 7,651.54 (-0.25%) while the drafted ES=F close is +0.10% (futures settle later in the session than the cash close); gold is up 0.29% on the drafted GC=F close but several wraps show gold lower on the day (about 4,168-4,185); votes use the drafted closes and avoid the conflicting levels.

High-yield OAS: govspending.org shows 3.02% on 28 September (2.80% on 24 September) while another source shows 2.73% for the month; no 30 September print was obtainable, so credit votes are neutral. AAII (32.7/19.2/48.1) is the survey for the week ending 23 September, the latest published as of 30 September. StoneX/CFTC dollar and Saxo gold positioning are for the week to 22 September. MOVE: 96.00 on 25 September in one source, nothing newer.

Fed odds: October hike probability fell to roughly 50% from over 70% after Williams' remarks on 30 September (news log, single source). Calendar: ISM manufacturing 1 October, jobs report 2 October. Seasonality votes are neutral because no dated sourced statistic was obtained.

News-log entries for 2026-09-30 (August PCE, Williams, Micron results, mixed close with 10-year at multi-decade high, Anthropic IPO/SpaceX compute deal) were already in data/news_log.json; the Artifact database returned the same five entries. No hand-entered issue entries were dated 30 September.

newsLog.numbers: Q4 revenue $54.23B (vs $41.46B in Q3, up ~381% y/y from $11.32B); non-GAAP EPS $33.42, GAAP EPS $32.87; Q1 FY27 guide: revenue $61.5B ±$1.5B, non-GAAP EPS $38.15 ±$1.00
newsLog.reaction: Shares rose after hours as strong revenue guidance offset a slight margin miss; lifted broader semiconductor/AI complex
newsLog.vsExp: Non-GAAP EPS ~$33.42 vs ~$31.56 est. (beat); revenue above high end of prior guidance

newsLog.event: Wall Street closed mixed: Dow fell on rotation out of cyclicals while Nasdaq edged higher and S&P slipped, as 10-year Treasury yields hit fresh multi-decade highs
newsLog.reaction: Tech outperformed (Intel +3.7% on AI-driven CPU demand) while cyclicals, financials and industrials lagged; rising yields pressured rate-sensitive sectors

newsLog.event: Anthropic's confidential IPO prospectus reportedly shows it could pay SpaceX up to $84.5B for computing capacity through 2029, nearly double the previously reported ~$45B figure
newsLog.reaction: SpaceX-linked shares rose ~2-3% on the disclosure; underscores scale of AI infrastructure spending ahead of Anthropic's planned IPO
